Hotels: 77% of revenue is online. Your reviews are your shop window

Only a few years ago, guests often chose their hotel by phone, through an agency or by walking up to the front desk. Today, the vast majority of bookings go through the internet. According to Statista's Hotels dossier, online channels accounted for 77% of worldwide hotel revenue in 2024.

This shift has a direct consequence: before booking, guests read. They compare photos, prices and above all the reviews left by those who stayed before them. For a hotel, those reviews have become the main shop window.

An online share that keeps growing

The increase has been steady for years. According to the dossier, the share of hotel revenue generated online rose from 66% in 2017 to 71% in 2020, then 76% in 2023 and 77% in 2024. Forecasts point to 80% in 2028 and 81% in 2030.

In other words, by the end of the decade, more than four dollars out of every five spent on hotels will come from an online booking. Traditional channels are not disappearing, but they are becoming a minority.

This shift affects every type of property, from large chains to independent hotels.

A growing market

The market itself keeps growing. Worldwide hotel segment revenue is estimated at $362.74 billion in 2025. According to the dossier's projections, it would grow by another $187.42 billion between 2025 and 2036.

Demand is there: the global hotel occupancy rate reached 70% in August 2026. In Europe, it stood at 76% that month, compared with 66% in the Americas. In this context, competition between properties largely plays out online, on the same results pages and the same platforms.

Price matters, experience decides

Travelers remain price-conscious. According to a global survey conducted in late 2024, price and value for money were the top priority for 55% of leisure travelers when choosing a hotel abroad, compared with 35% of business travelers.

But value for money is not judged on price alone. It is judged on what other guests say about their stay. Two hotels at the same rate are not equal if one keeps collecting comments about noise or cleanliness and the other compliments about the welcome.

That is why reviews carry so much weight: they are the only independent information future guests have about the real quality of what they are about to pay for.

Reviews, information worth using

For a hotelier, reviews play a double role. They influence future guests, and they tell the property what works and what disappoints. That second role is often underused: reviews are read one by one, as they arrive, and answered when there is time.

Yet hundreds of reviews spread across several platforms contain very rich information. Read together, they show which topics come up, which are improving and which are getting worse. Read one by one, they get lost.

As we saw in another article, few hoteliers see most of their guests return: what those guests write often explains why.

Replying to reviews also matters: future guests read the replies, and a calm, specific answer to a complaint often reassures more than a perfect score.

Analyzing every review, property by property

Automatic language analysis can read every review and comment, whatever the platform, and sort them by theme: room, bedding, cleanliness, noise, breakfast, welcome, location, value for money. For each theme, it measures the dominant tone and how it changes.

A hotel manager then knows exactly what pushes their rating up or down, and can focus first on what matters most to guests. A group can compare its properties and share good practices. Our hospitality and restaurants page gives examples.

The analysis relies on models such as Mistral, BERT, Llama, GPT or Claude depending on the case, and data stays hosted in France.

Taking care of the shop window

When 77% of revenue comes through digital channels, online reputation is no longer a communication topic: it is a commercial one. Every pain point fixed improves future reviews, and every better review weighs on the next bookings.

Properties that track their reviews as a management indicator, just like occupancy rate or average daily rate, have a lasting advantage over those that simply reply to them.

What this means for you

In hospitality, 77% of revenue now comes through digital channels, and your reviews are your shop window. custovox.ai reads all of them, by theme and by property, to show you what raises or lowers your reputation.
